protocol.title: PE beads · Exp 01 · Laser power at the sample
protocol.summary: Measure 561 nm power at the sample through the 10x and 20x against the NIS laser %, and pick the powers that keep PE linear.

children.body: Every later experiment is specified in µW at the sample, never in laser %.

chips.text: ≈45 min first time, 5 min per session after

children.body: Pins: peak irradiance at the focus, and from it the PE excitation rate, the saturation level and the bleaching dose per frame. The same laser % gives different power through the 10x and the 20x because the back aperture is filled differently, and the %-to-µW map drifts during a session.

Model prediction: with confocal weighting the image is 5 % below linear at I/Iₛ ≈ 0.08, which is ≈2 µW at the sample through the 20x and ≈6–7 µW through the 10x (Iₛ ≈ 19 kW/cm² for R-PE at 561 nm). The beam-centre number in the calculator is the worst case; the whole image is ≈0.6–0.67 of it.
≈45 min first time; 5 min at the start and end of each quantitative session.

rows.free_text: Slide-format photodiode power sensor (Thorlabs S170C-type) and console
NIS-Elements with the 561 nm line enabled

children.body: Acquisition settings

rows.value: 10x/0.45 Plan Apo λD, then the 20x (read the NA on the barrel)
Stationary spot (point or stimulation mode) if NIS allows; otherwise a 512² scan at maximum zoom, and note that the reading is scan-averaged

children.body: Before any quantitative acquisition: stand and lasers on for 2–3 h; 561 nm excitation; the same PE emission band (e.g. 570–620 nm) every time; 16-bit with fine integration (the default is 12-bit, so check the file); one HV and one offset for the whole session; background mode at least 50 DN above zero; no saturated pixels. Record the transmitted-light channel with every PE frame: beads are found in it, never in PE. Find focus in transmitted light and hold it with Perfect Focus. Never live-scan PE to focus.

attrs.label: Irradiance and PE saturation at the focus

outputs.name: sublin_pct
outputs.label: Emission below linear at the beam centre

children.body: With [!var:p_uw] at NA [!var:na] the peak irradiance is [!var:i0_kw] and PE emission is [!var:sublin_pct] below linear. The power for I/Iₛ = [!var:target_s] is [!var:p_target_uw].
Set up
Switch the 561 nm laser on at least 30 min before measuring, for a stable output.
With the laser off, zero the meter. Set its wavelength to 561 nm.
Put the sensor on the stage, centred under the 10x, with its active area at the focus (focus on the sensor surface in transmitted light).
Power ladder
Park the beam (stationary spot) or start a 512² scan at maximum zoom. Read µW at each laser %: 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100.
Read 0 % again at the end, to catch meter drift.
Swap to the 20x, refocus on the sensor, and repeat the ladder.
A scanned beam is blanked during flyback, so a scanning reading is lower than the on-time power. Use a stationary spot when you can, and always note which mode you used.
Every quantitative session
Read the % you will use (and one higher point) through the objective you will use, at the start and at the end of the session. A change of more than 5 % means the intensities need a drift correction.
Fit µW = a × (laser %) per objective over the linear part of the ladder; record a and the 20x/10x ratio at the same %.
Enter the measured µW in the calculator with each objective's NA, and read the % that gives the target I/Iₛ (0.08).
Decision: the laser % that gives the operating power for each objective (1–2 µW through the 20x, ≈6 µW through the 10x, unless Exp 07 moves them). Record power in µW in every later plate map.
Record for every acquisition
